questions.question: You ran batched backfills on tables with a billion rows. How did you choose the batch size, and how did you know it was safe to continue?
evidence: Wrote goose migrations for production, including batched backfills on tables with 1B rows
questions.why: Tests the scale claim and her judgement under load.
follow_ups: What would you monitor while it ran?
warning_signs: fixed batch size with no reasoning

questions.question: Most of our backend is Python with SQLAlchemy. What Python have you written, and how would you get productive in an ORM-based codebase?
questions.why: Her CV shows Go with pgx and sqlc, and Python only for scripting; the rubric credits Go as transferable.
follow_ups: What do you expect to miss from sqlc, and what would you watch out for in an ORM?
listen_for: awareness of ORM pitfalls like N+1
warning_signs: dismisses the language switch as trivial without specifics

questions.question: Who ran the PostgreSQL servers in your current team? Which parts of their operation have you done yourself?
questions.why: Her CV doesn't show backups, pooling or replication work.
follow_ups: What would you want to learn first if you owned them?
warning_signs: claims operations experience but can't describe any

notes_for_interviewer: Go background: judge Python and ORM skills as learnable, per the rubric; focus on depth in migrations and performance.
